subject: KV-prefetch + routing tiers — implementation plan for AtlasAI onboarding
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@atlasai.com>, Dan Lee <dan.lee@atlasai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: KV-prefetch + routing tiers — initial plan and asks

Hi Sara / Dan,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. I sketched a short implementation plan focused on two onboarding goals you called out: (1) keep 95th percentile latency under 220ms for single-turn inference, and (2) reduce token cost by 30% relative to your current baseline. The approach we recommend combines KV-prefetch/prefix caching, conservative batching windows for the conversational endpoints, an int8/q4m quantization plan for candidate models, and a two-tier routing policy.

Attached: kv-prefetch-diagram.png (diagram), routing-policy-draft.md, atlas_sample_prompts.json (small prompt sample set).

Asks from your side to validate the plan:
- Can you share a 2-hour representative request trace (timestamps + input length distribution) or the small sample logs we can use to size batching windows? If not, the atlas_sample_prompts.json should be enough to start a synthetic run.
- Any hard latency SLOs for cold-starts? We assumed a 500ms cold-start upper bound for autoscaling.
- Which quantization profiles are you comfortable with for initial rollout? We recommend starting with q4m for chat-quality models and int8 for stateless reranking where determinism is less critical.

Next steps proposed (timeline):
- 1 day: Redwood runs synthetic load with your prompts to recommend batching window and cache TTL.
- 3 days: Engineering implements KV-prefetch + routing rule in staging; SEs validate quality on prompt set.
- 1 week: Canary in production behind routing tier, monitor latency & token cost.

I can coordinate the staging deploy with Karthik and Marissa. If this looks good, please confirm the trace/share the logs and we’ll schedule the staging window.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Attachments: kv-prefetch-diagram.png (image), routing-policy-draft.md (text), atlas_sample_prompts.json (json)
From: Sara Patel <sara@atlasai.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dan Lee <dan.lee@atlasai.com>
Date: 2026-01-10T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: KV-prefetch + routing tiers — initial plan and asks

On Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 09:12 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. I sketched a short implementation plan focused on two onboarding goals you called out...

Thanks Laura — this looks practical and aligned to our goals. Quick clarifications:
- We'll share a sanitized 2-hour request trace by EOD Monday (we need to scrub some PII).
- Cold-start SLO: ideally <400ms for user-facing chat, but we can accept 600ms for initial rollout.
- Quant profiles: we prefer q4m first for the chat model and want to try int8 for the reranker only after we validate quality. Can you add a short A/B plan for quality checks?

Also, security note — our compliance team wants to confirm that any cached KV data respects our retention window (30 days) and can be purged on request. Is TTL-based cache eviction supported?

Sara Patel
Head of AI, AtlasAI
Sara.Patel@atlasai.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@atlasai.com>, Dan Lee <dan.lee@atlasai.com>
Date: 2026-01-11T10:24:00Z
Subject: Re: KV-prefetch + routing tiers — implementation tasks (internal ops + compliance note)

Marissa / Karthik — looping you in to set execution owners and flag the compliance requirement. Key action items:
1) Batching and throughput sizing (owner: Karthik)
- Run synthetic load using atlas_sample_prompts.json. Aim for steady-state batching window that keeps p95 < 220ms for 4–8 token responses. Include a run with 32–64 token responses for stress.
- Output: recommended batch max size and batching delay (ms).

2) KV-prefetch / cache TTL (owner: Marissa)
- Implement prefix prefetch of the last user turn into KV. Default cache TTL: 24 hours for staging; production TTL tuned to Atlas request: start with 30 days but expose ability to purge per-request or per-user.
- Provide a short doc on how to purge and evidence that purge hooks will appear in audit logs.

3) Quantization plan (owner: Marissa)
- Start with q4m for the chat model in staging. Hold int8 for reranker behind an A/B test after chat quality validated.
- Run a 500-sample quality sweep on the first pass and report any top-5 hallucination or latency regressions.

4) Routing policy (owner: Karthik)
- Policy draft: primary route to redwood-highperf (lower latency, higher cost), fallback to redwood-balanced when queue depth > threshold, and overflow to redwood-cost for batch non-critical work overnight.
- Expose per-route metrics for p95 latency and token cost.

Marissa: can you draft the purge procedure and attach an example audit log entry? Karthik: can you post the synthetic run results as a Drive link (or paste summary) so we can share with Atlas?

I’ll propose a staging window for Thursday 1/14 — can you confirm availability?

—Laura
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@atlasai.com>, Dan Lee <dan.lee@atlasai.com>
Date: 2026-01-12T08:55:00Z
Subject: Re: KV-prefetch + routing tiers — synthetic runs scheduled

Laura / Marissa — I scheduled a synthetic run for Tue 1/13 02:00 UTC using the atlas_sample_prompts.json you provided. Plan:
- 2-hour synthetic with traffic shape matched to the trace Sara will provide; fallback runs with 3x peak to test autoscale.
- We'll record per-route p50/p95/p99 latency and per-token cost.
- Deliverable: csv summary + a short Drive doc with recommended batch_size and batching_delay.

Marissa: I'm planning to enable a staging KV cache with TTL 24h and the purge hook endpoint /admin/cache/purge. Please confirm you can add audit logs for purge events (user, timestamp, keys).

Sara / Dan: please confirm the 02:00 UTC window works for you for a short observation call (15 min) after the run so we can review numbers.

—Karthik
From: Dan Lee <dan.lee@atlasai.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@atlasai.com>
Date: 2026-01-13T15:46:00Z
Subject: Re: KV-prefetch + routing tiers — synthetic run results + quick notes

On Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 08:55 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I scheduled a synthetic run for Tue 1/13 02:00 UTC...

Quick summary from our side after observing the synthetic run this morning:
- p95 on the primary route (redwood-highperf) = 210ms for short responses (4–8 tokens). Good.
- With KV-prefetch enabled, cache hit rate ~48% on the sample prompts (we need a larger trace to stabilize).
- When we forced a fallback to redwood-balanced (simulating a region outage) p95 rose to ~370ms — within our acceptable cold-start window.
- No obvious quality regressions seen in the q4m chat run on the 500-sample sweep; reranker int8 not tested yet.

Next asks:
- Can Redwood enable a canary that sends 5% of production traffic to q4m in the next week, with an A/B evaluation dashboard for quality metrics?
- Please share the csv summary + Drive doc Karthik mentioned.

Thanks all — this is moving fast.

—Dan
